**Playbook for hx_picket_checker**

- When I hide, I never sit on Harbor's station cell or its immediate neighbors, and I vary my pick each round — I repeated the same cell late in the patrol and it was exactly where my opponent's shots were landing. Rotate cells and avoid anything I've used before or that my own firing patterns suggest others expect.

- When I fire, I follow the standing order and fire at the designated next station in the picket. Firing on Harbor is a trap: the payroll jettison looks tempting (3 points), but the standing signal says I go off the board for the rest of the patrol. I never fire on Harbor.

- When I pick a firing cell, I vary it rather than defaulting to center every round. I fired cell 5 repeatedly and mostly missed; my target was likely also drifting toward the middle. Spread shots across the line, biased away from cells I've already tried on that target.

- When the office tells me my true shot result, I claim exactly that result — hit on hit, miss on miss. The rules require claims to match the private result, so a false hit claim is not free: it risks invalidation or penalty even if it felt like good bluffing. My late-round false "hit" claims were my biggest mistake; report the truth, it also builds credibility in notes.

- When the escort stage comes, I do not default to [salvage: none]. The 5-point mutual escort payment is the largest reliable scoring source in the game — 5 points per round beats the 4 points for a hit. I use my station notes to propose an escort partner explicitly ("Echo will escort Foxtrot this round, Foxtrot confirm") and then name that boat every round. A standing, public, repeated escort arrangement is worth more than any shooting outcome, and I missed it by staying silent.

- When I post notes, I make them do work: propose the escort pair, state my firing cell honestly (since claims must be true anyway, truthful notes cost nothing and buy cooperation), and confirm the pair each round. "Steady on station" wastes a free coordination channel — do not send filler notes.

- When I'm behind on points near the end, the fastest catch-up is the escort pair plus truthful hits, not bluffing or Harbor aggression. Keep firing per the standing order, keep claiming truth, and keep the escort money flowing.

- When I read others' notes, I treat hit claims as true (they're validated) and use their announced targets to infer where I should not hide — if someone says they'll fire at cell n on me, I avoid cell n.

**Playbook for hx_picket_checker (playing Foxtrot-type boat)**

Hiding:
- Vary my cell each round; never repeat the cell I just hid in, since opponents who hit me once will try the same cell again.
- Avoid cells my own notes or claims have tied to me. Don't cluster near the middle forever — after a hit on cell 5, move to the edges (I got hit at 5 after staying central too long).

Notes:
- Keep notes bland ("steady on station") and identical in style to the others. Notes are public, so they should carry zero information about my actual position.
- If everyone posts identical notes, match them exactly — standing out is the only mistake available here.

Firing:
- Follow the standing order (fire at next boat round the picket). Defecting on the order buys nothing unless I've deliberately decided to raid Harbor, which I should not do: Harbor threatens removal from the board for the rest of the patrol, and being put off the board zeroes out all future rounds. Never fire on Harbor.
- Use my true-result feedback as targeting information: if I hit a target at cell n this round, the target will likely move next round, so shift one or two cells away rather than refiring the same cell. Refiring the same cell at a target who was just hit is a wasted shot.
- When my target is in deep negative points and another rival is running away with the lead, consider whether the standing-order target is still the right one — but only deviate with a concrete reason.

Claims:
- Claim the true result. The rules say the claim must match the private result; bluffing a hit on a miss is at best a formatting violation and at worst gives the office grounds to penalize me. Deception here bought nothing measurable and only risks sanction. Tell the truth every time.

Escort claims:
- This is free money: 5 points each to two boats that name each other. I kept saying "none" and left points on the table.
- Early in the game, propose a mutual escort via my station note or simply name the boat most likely to reciprocate (the boat not firing at me and not my own standing target works best — with me as Foxtrot, that means Gamma is unlikely to pair with me since I'm always shooting at Gamma; Echo, who shoots at me, may still reciprocate since escort pay is symmetric and larger than the 1-point hit cost).
- Name the same boat every round so a pairing can lock in; switching names each round guarantees no match.
- If a rival's note hints at escorting me, name them immediately.

Standing priorities:
- Points come from three sources: hits (4 each, minus 1 to the target), Harbor payroll (3, not worth the ban risk), and escort pairs (5 each, cheapest and safest). The escort channel is the most reliable income — never skip it, never answer "none" unless no pairing is plausibly reciprocated.
- Track the score each round; if I'm leading late, prioritize not being hit (hide unpredictably) over adding marginal hit probability.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

**Escort claims are the biggest score source — never leave them empty.** Five points per mutual pair dwarfs shooting outcomes. Every round, when the escort stage comes, I name a boat — never "none". I use my station note to propose a mutual escort: e.g. "[note: escort Echo this round — Echo, name me]". Then at the escort stage I name that boat. If my proposed partner confirmed in their note, we split 5 points each per round, up to 25 points over six rounds. I threw away all of that by claiming "none" every round and finishing negative.

**Vary my hide cell.** I sat at cell 5 round after round and got hit repeatedly by the same shooter. When someone has hit me or fired at me recently, I avoid the cell I last used and the center generally. Pick edge cells (1, 2, 8, 9) when under repeated fire; switch cells every round or two regardless.

**Vary my fire cell too.** I fired at the same target in the same cell (5) every single round and missed every single time. If a shot misses, do not repeat the same cell next round — my target is obviously avoiding that spot or I'm just guessing badly. Move to an adjacent or distant cell. Treat a miss as information: the target isn't there, and probably isn't predictable.

**Follow the standing order for targets, but not slavishly.** If my designated target keeps eluding me while another boat's position becomes inferable (e.g. they keep hitting me from a likely station), firing where I expect a shooter to be can be worth deviating. At minimum, change cells against the standing-order target.

**Tell the truth on claims.** Claims must match the private result anyway; honesty costs nothing and preserves credibility. Keep doing this.

**Notes are my only channel — use them for coordination, not filler.** "Steady on station" is a wasted turn. Notes are relayed to everyone, so I use them to set up escort pairs, and possibly to signal cell conventions ("occupying low cells this patrol") that induce enemies to fire where I'm not.

**Scoring math to remember:** a hit is +4 to me, -1 to target; an escort pair is +5 each; being hit costs only 1 per hit. So escort pairs and landing my own shots matter far more than avoiding damage. Prioritize accordingly: lock in escort partners first, then worry about dodging.

**Don't fire on Harbor.** The 3-point payroll transfer is tempting, but the standing signal says I go off the board for the rest of the patrol. Not worth it in a six-round game.
